_what: Throughline's rules as data: the single source that the handoff checker (tools/handoff.py), a project's own gates and the flow's build script all read. The prose in SKILL.md and references/ explains these rules; this file is what is checked.

_fields.kind: core (the task track itself) | step (a fixed point of the wrap or the boot) | hook | path-rule | identity
_fields.enforced_by: [{file, state: built | planned | none}] - file null with state none means only the agent's own discipline holds it
_fields.pass_condition: an observable fact that shows the rule was kept
_fields.why: {ruling, incident, source[]} - the decision, what went wrong without it, where it is explained
_fields.written_in: [{file, anchor}] - where the prose states it; anchor null until that text is written

main.means: the goal anchor; exactly one live at a time

subtask.means: a subtask of the current MAIN (membership); stacks with an origin icon

origin.🍏: surfaced this session; in no plan or log yet
origin.🍋: logged before, and came back or was pulled in

kind.rule: at most one per row, after the origin icon; chosen so its meaning is obvious without a legend

icons.stacking: membership first, then origin, then kind: 🔸🍋🐛 · a task serving no MAIN keeps its origin icon alone

handoff.section_match: a heading counts as a section when its text after any leading marker STARTS with the section name, or when it ENDS with the alias

carried.means: moved to a named row or file

dropped.means: left out on the human's own words

row_ref.placement: the item ends with ' · <row ID or path>'

brief.words: letters-only words on the same line, the ID tokens not counted

module_schema._what: the shape of a project module (the project's own wrap or boot steps); the runner that executes modules comes in 0.4

fields.trigger: when it runs: {always: true} or {event: [...]} (e.g. engine changed, a protected file moved)
fields.depends_on: ids of modules that must run first
fields.pass: the pass criteria, fixed in the module, not chosen at run time
fields.skipped_when: a condition under which the module is not needed; a module skipped as not needed satisfies its dependents

module_schema.today_keyed_on: the session number, not the calendar date

rules.text: Exactly one ⭐️ MAIN is live at a time; more than one MAIN in a session is normal, each confirmed by the human.
rules.pass_condition: the handoff holds exactly one line that starts with ⭐️, [MAIN] or main_goal: true

why.ruling: maintainers, 2026-09-29: several MAINs per session are normal, one ⭐️ live at a time
why.incident: a task list with two anchors gives the agent no single thing to check itself against

rules.text: The MAIN is written at an observable moment: the first action that is not answering a question; with no MAIN then, stop, propose one and ask the human to confirm.
rules.pass_condition: a handoff whose Done lists work also lists a MAIN or a zero-MAIN declaration

why.ruling: maintainers, 2026-09-29: key the anchor on an event the agent can see, not on 'once the goal is clear'
why.incident: an agent's proposed MAIN was answered with a question, not a confirm; it then ran about 130 tool calls with no MAIN and no task list

written_in.anchor: the first action that is not answering a question

rules.text: A MAIN's title is frozen when the human confirms it; the verdict is given under that title, and a redirect is a new MAIN, not a rename.
rules.pass_condition: each MAIN in Done carries the title it was confirmed under

why.ruling: Throughline 0.1: the title is frozen at confirm time
why.incident: a goal quietly renamed into whatever happened makes 'done' unfalsifiable

written_in.anchor: the title is frozen at confirm

rules.text: Once a MAIN is confirmed it is broken into 🔸 subtasks, worked one by one; every MAIN in Done lists at least one.
rules.pass_condition: every '### MAIN' entry in Done is followed by at least one '- 🔸' line

why.ruling: maintainers, 2026-09-29: 🔸 marks a subtask of the MAIN
why.incident: a MAIN with no parts cannot show which part is still open

rules.text: A MAIN is LANDED only when every one of its subtasks is done.
rules.pass_condition: no LANDED MAIN in Done has a subtask that is carried, dropped or without a status

why.ruling: maintainers, 2026-09-29: a MAIN is complete only when every subtask is done
why.incident: MAINs closed as done while a part was still open; the open part was lost with the next session

rules.text: A subtask leaves the list in one of three ways only: done (closed by a passing test), carried to a named row or file, or dropped on the human's own words.
rules.pass_condition: every '- 🔸' line in Done ends in done, in carried → <row ID or path>, or in dropped · human: "<words>"

why.ruling: maintainers, 2026-10-07: a red is closed by a passing test, not dropped
why.incident: a deliverable narrowed to its open checks, one check was closed, and the item fell out of the queue with none of the three - it was found weeks later

written_in.anchor: leaves the list three ways only

rules.text: A session that changes no file may run with no MAIN, and only on the human's own words, recorded in Done as zero-MAIN.
rules.pass_condition: a handoff with no MAIN entry carries 'zero-MAIN · human: "<words>"' in Done

why.ruling: maintainers, 2026-09-29: any session that changes a file belongs to a MAIN; only a pure question-and-answer session may run without one, on the human's words
why.incident: work done outside any MAIN has no verdict and no owner at the next start

rules.text: Icons stack in a fixed order: 🔸 membership, then the origin icon (🌶️ 🍏 🍋), then an optional kind icon whose meaning is obvious at a glance.
rules.pass_condition: a task row reads membership, origin, kind in that order, e.g. 🔸🍋🐛

why.ruling: maintainers, 2026-09-29: 🔸 says which MAIN, 🌶️/🍏/🍋 say where it came from; 2026-10-13: a kind icon is kept because the human reads it at a glance
why.incident: 🌶️ was defined as 'in service of the MAIN', mixing origin with membership

rules.text: The task list lives where the human sees it - the host's task tool and plan pane, or else the board or file the human watches - and the MAIN reaches it at the confirm instant, not at the wrap.
rules.pass_condition: the MAIN is visible in the human's task surface within the turn it was confirmed

why.ruling: maintainers, 2026-10-07: with no task UI, the board is the task surface
why.incident: the human asked whether the MAIN was on the board; it was not until a later step

rules.text: Every next action and every ruling not yet in its home file has its own durable row (a board row or a plan file); the handoff only points at it.
rules.pass_condition: every item in Next actions and in Rulings not yet home ends with a row ID or a file path, or the block says none

why.ruling: maintainers, 2026-10-07: six blocks and one rule - every block-3 and block-6 item has a durable row
why.incident: work that lived only in a newest-only 'next' list was lost twice when a session pivot overwrote the list

written_in.anchor: the handoff only points at it

rules.text: The pass condition of a check is written before the check runs, and the row is verified only by that check.
rules.pass_condition: the two-box row names its check and its expected result before the run

why.ruling: maintainers, 2026-10-07: changes are closed only after a test passes; the condition comes first
why.incident: a condition chosen after the run fits whatever the run printed

written_in.anchor: the pass condition is written before the check runs

rules.text: A handoff carries six blocks - machine fields, where this session stopped, next actions, waiting on others, project state, rulings not yet home - plus the Goal, Done and Re-derive on pickup.
rules.pass_condition: handoff.py check finds every section of handoff.sections

why.ruling: maintainers, 2026-10-07: the handoff skeleton is six blocks and one rule
why.incident: of one measured handoff, only the state sections were read by scripts; the rest was rules and history loaded at every start

written_in.anchor: sections a handoff must have are listed in rules/task-rules.json

rules.text: The ⭐️ Goal of a handoff is a proposal the human confirms at the next start, and it is the first Next action, not a second list.
rules.pass_condition: the Goal text equals the first Next action's text

why.ruling: maintainers, 2026-10-12: the Goal is Next actions #1
why.incident: a plan copied forward word for word as if decided, though the human had not confirmed it

written_in.anchor: must equal the first item of Next actions

rules.text: Each MAIN's verdict has one home, Done; Machine fields carries a generated copy that must agree.
rules.pass_condition: every '- verdict' line in Machine fields matches its MAIN in Done

why.ruling: maintainers, 2026-10-12: Done is the home; Machine fields a generated copy
why.incident: two homes for one fact drift apart

rules.text: A section is found by its name - the heading text after any marker starts with it - or by the alias '· Throughline: <name>' at the end of a project's own heading.
rules.pass_condition: a heading that merely contains the name inside another word does not count

why.ruling: maintainers, 2026-09-29: match the name, not a word inside another heading; annotate a project heading, don't rename it
why.incident: a substring match let 'State' be satisfied by an engine-state heading and 'Open / Next' by a list of open questions - the opposite of a next-steps list

rules.text: The wrap runs seven steps in order: ask before wrapping; a verdict per MAIN; close the task list and its rows with the verdicts; write the session log (one file plus an index line); rewrite the handoff; run the checks; name the session, then the final report.
rules.pass_condition: the wrap's transcript shows the seven steps in order

why.ruling: maintainers, 2026-10-07: the handoff half is a skeleton every project shares plus project modules
why.incident: five measured wraps ran the same steps in different orders and skipped different ones

rules.text: At the start, copy the next-actions list verbatim before any work (the queue freeze) and write the session-start brief to disk beside it.
rules.pass_condition: a frozen queue file and a brief file exist for the session

why.ruling: maintainers, 2026-10-07: the queue freeze is skeleton, not project; the start brief becomes a file
why.incident: a brief that is not a file cannot be checked; an item fell out of a queue nobody had frozen

written_in.anchor: write the session-start brief to disk

rules.text: An ID never stands alone: in the session-start brief, every ID-like token carries words saying what it is.

event: the next session start reads the previous brief

rules.pass_condition: handoff.py brief prints no WARN for the brief

why.ruling: maintainers, 2026-09-29: a short code travels with its owner's name on first use
why.incident: a handoff carried 'D.5 two questions' for three weeks with nothing saying what D.5 was

rules.text: A project's own wrap or boot steps are modules in one schema: a trigger, dependencies, pass criteria fixed in the module, a not-needed condition that satisfies dependents, a breaker of 3.
rules.pass_condition: each project module validates against module_schema

why.ruling: maintainers, 2026-10-07: the circuit breaker is 3; 'today' keys on the session number
why.incident: a project step written nowhere was found only by a red check, twice

written_in.anchor: a project's own steps are modules

rules.text: A handoff is shareable: no keys, tokens, passwords or personal data; the checker warns on obvious patterns, and real redaction is the writer's.
rules.pass_condition: handoff.py check prints no 'possible leaked secret' warning

why.ruling: Throughline 0.1: a heuristic backstop, never a pass
why.incident: a regex can never catch every secret, so a hit is a warning and the human reviews
